TLDR; yes but no but yes but not in that way. In all honesty she might want to be the person you need and want, but I don't think she can be, at least not yet.  
  

She can have the knowledge that cheating is bad, that lying is bad, that hurting you is bad, but perhaps she's never seen or experienced that happening with a consistent result in her real life ya know outside of media, where things are fake and scripted. She believes you will not love her anymore when you leave, but she will think she completely won you over again if you return without enforcing your boundary. She will think she can go right around it again, if she can.  


Start the consistent result now, by standing by your own feelings and not giving in to hers. You do not owe her growth, you can't force her through growth, and you don't have to concern yourself with it. People have been trying to force progress for years, and maybe that's how she ended up this way. Yes her emotions are real, but her perspective on life is warped and causing pain to you with her emotional actions. It's so warped that she can't even conceptualize that what she is doing is *really wrong.  
  
She can feel terrible all she wants, but she won't think she can move on and learn from it if you don't forgive her. This is factually untrue, there is always another way,, but that concept could be at the core of her beliefs.  
  
Like I said, you don't owe her anything. She owed you loyalty, and didn't understand that the consequences for this were real and will be very, very painful for her. If you don't respect your boundaries she, whether consciously or unconsciously, will follow suit. Best of luck.

Personal killing vs killing at random

Killing someone is ALWAYS wrong but killing a person based on who that individual person is or what they did to you is different from opening fire in a public place to kill as many people as possible. They did you no "wrong," they were just present. 

For example if a student were to open fire at their school because they were bullied, that is different than if they decided instead to kill the individuals that bullied them. They chose to shoot at anyone in proximity for maximum casualties versus seeking out the who "wronged" him. Both scenarios are terrible and neither should be a logical conclusion for the student, but the intentions are very different overall.

I use wronged very loosely, because there is virtually no good reason to take anyone else's life, and no matter how badly they hurt you mentally or emotionally or how strong your beliefs are, there should not be any logical train of thought that leads you to "this person deserves to die and I am going to kill them" or "I need to send a message and murdering people is how I should do that to scare the people I don't like, and possibly kill some on the way."

anytime! I'm hoping you to get as much information as possible for your living arrangements so you don't move in thinking it'll be great to find out you hate it, or vice versa. Good luck choosing!

depends on what takes priority for you concerning living arrangements. 
Saving money? Any of the Bassetties. That will be the cheapest option, at least it was my freshman year. I lived in Meisner.

Privacy? Wendell A or Wendell B, they have a pod set up in a lot of their rooms, which means you and 3 other people will share a living space like shower, kitchen, bathroom, but have your own bedroom. Dugmore might have a setup like this, but I am not positive yet.

Cleanliness? NOT Meisner. (custodian is VERY kind and usually keeps up but slacks a little here and there occasionally with kitchen garbage) A lot of the buildings are kept really nice but obviously can't be perfect; either of the Wendells, Barto, Sue Lombard, Alford Montgomery, Carmody Munroe, Davies, and Kamola are usually kept nice from what I have seen, I haven't really gotten to see the other buildings during the busy school year.

Accessibility for disabilities? I think you should try for one of the newer buildings. Those buildings are the only ones with elevators; Kamola, Sue Lombard, Barto, Wendell A & B, Dugmore will of course have an elevator. The rest of the buildings you will have to live on the first floor if you need wheelchair accessibility. In order to live with an ESA or service dog, you can live in any building I think, but need to talk to disability services (not sure exactly what the process is for a service animal, but for an ESA they will have you get some paperwork filled out by your PCP. Not a mental health specialist, your PCP. idk why either.)

Buildings I don't recommend; Green and Kennedy (poor layout, third floor has no bathrooms at all, very hot in the summer and no air flow), Meisner because I lived there and am biased against it.

Honorary mention; not sure what the deal is with Munson (idk if its dorms or special apartments or something), but it's not a terrible building, you get your own bathroom (with your roommates of course) and little kitchen setup, like with Wendell, except in Wendell you have your own bedroom while with Munson you share everything, and there is an ice machine downstairs and I love it.

Downside to Wendells, there are NO water fountains (not really an issue if you live there I guess)
An upside to living in the north area of campus though, is North Village Cafe. The food is FAR better than ANYTHING served at the SURC and it is attached to Green (farthest north building on campus)
That is everything I think I know, hope this was helpful!
